Do NOT touch kamal/deploys/dev _build.

MCP note: on "No session_id available" add session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8"; if MCP hangs >2 min, message me and keep coding.

DESIGN (standard LiveView + Payment Element flow):
1. Gateway: add create_payment_intent WITHOUT confirm (new function or a :confirm option) returning {:ok, %{id, client_secret, status}}. Live: POST /v1/payment_intents with amount/currency/automatic_payment_methods[enabled]=true&allow_redirects=never, NO confirm/payment_method — return client_secret. Test adapter: fabricate id + client_secret ("pi_test_..._secret_test"). Keep the existing confirmed-path function for /pay/:token card-on-file (unchanged).
2. Booking flow: when the client reaches the confirm step (policy checkbox page), on "confirm_booking" WITH policy agreed: create the unconfirmed intent, persist it on the lead (status payment_pending as today), and render the payment step: a form with the Stripe Payment Element mounted via a JS hook + "Pay $X" button. Pass publishable key + client_secret via data attributes. On payment_confirmed event just show the existing payment_pending state — the WEBHOOK (payment_intent.succeeded, already wired) converts the lead; the accept page already handles the converted state on remount. BONUS if cheap: subscribe the LiveView to a PubSub topic broadcast from the webhook conversion path so the page flips to confirmed live; otherwise a 3s poll of lead status while on payment_pending.
3. Config plumbing: runtime.exs prod block reads STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (already seeded in SSM on UAT) into config :cleaner_crm, :stripe_publishable_key; dev/test config nil. FALLBACK BEHAVIOR (critical for tests): when publishable key is NIL (dev/test), keep TODAY's flow exactly — hidden pm_card_visa field + server-side confirmed intent — so all 143 spex (849 especially) and LiveView tests stay green unmodified. The Elements path only renders when the key is configured.
4. Webhook: verify payment_intent.succeeded conversion works for UNCONFIRMED-then-client-confirmed intents identically (it keys off the intent id — should already).

Verify: MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean; FULL PORT=4002 MIX_ENV=test mix test green (308+, kill port 4002 first); FULL PORT=4002 mix spex green (143); mix assets.build succeeds (hook compiles); mix format. Add tests for the gateway no-confirm function (Test adapter) and the key-nil fallback rendering.

38	  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live do
  @moduledoc """
  Talks to the real Stripe API over `Req` and verifies webhook
  signatures per Stripe's documented scheme (HMAC-SHA256 over
  `"{timestamp}.{raw body}"`, compared against the `Stripe-Signature`
  header).

  Requires `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (see
  `.code_my_spec/integrations/stripe.md`). Verifying the signature
  needs the exact raw request bytes, which normal body parsing
  discards — `CleanerCrmWeb.CacheBodyReader` stashes them into
  `conn.assigns[:raw_body]` for the webhook route specifically.

  Missing credentials are a recoverable operational condition, not a
  bug: `create_payment_intent/1` returns `{:error, %{"code" =>
  "not_configured", ...}}` and `verify_webhook_event/1` returns
  `{:error, :invalid_signature}` rather than raising, so a deploy
  without keys degrades to a friendly error for the caller instead of
  crashing the LiveView or returning a raw 500 from the public
  `/pay/:token` or `/webhooks/stripe` endpoints. `config/dev.exs`
  avoids this entirely by defaulting to `StripeGateway.Test` — dev
  machines don't carry these secrets.
  """

  @behaviour CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway

  @base_url "https://api.stripe.com/v1"

  @impl true
  def create_payment_intent(
        %{amount_cents: amount_cents, payment_method: payment_method} = params
      ) do
    with {:ok, key} <- fetch_secret_key() do
      body =
        %{
          "amount" => amount_cents,
          "currency" => "usd",
          "payment_method" => payment_method,
          "confirm" => true,
          "off_session" => Map.get(params, :off_session, false),
          # Card-only, no redirect-based methods: confirming
          # server-side without a return_url requires redirects off.
          "automatic_payment_methods[enabled]" => true,
          "automatic_payment_methods[allow_redirects]" => "never"
        }
        |> put_metadata(Map.get(params, :metadata, %{}))

      @base_url
      |> Kernel.<>("/payment_intents")
      |> Req.post(form: body, auth: {:bearer, key})
      |> handle_response()
    end
  end

  # A misconfigured deploy (secret unset) is a recoverable operational
  # condition here, not a bug — callers already handle `{:error, _}` by
  # showing the payer/owner a friendly message, so this must never raise.
  defp fetch_secret_key do
    case secret_key() do
      nil ->
        {:error,
         %{"code" => "not_configured", "message" => "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not configured"}}

      key ->
        {:ok, key}
    end
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{status: status, body: %{"id" => id, "status" => stripe_status}}})
       when status in 200..299 do
    {:ok, %{id: id, status: stripe_status}}
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{body: %{"error" => error}}}), do: {:error, error}

  defp handle_response({:error, reason}),
    do: {:error, %{"code" => "request_failed", "message" => inspect(reason)}}

  defp put_metadata(body, metadata) do
    Enum.reduce(metadata, body, fn {key, value}, acc ->
      Map.put(acc, "metadata[#{key}]", to_string(value))
    end)
  end

  @impl true
  def verify_webhook_event(conn) do
    with {:ok, secret} <- fetch_webhook_secret(),
         [signature_header] <- Plug.Conn.get_req_header(conn, "stripe-signature"),
         raw_body when is_binary(raw_body) <- conn.assigns[:raw_body],
         {:ok, timestamp, expected_signature} <- parse_signature_header(signature_header),
         true <- Plug.Crypto.secure_compare(sign(secret, timestamp, raw_body), expected_signature) do
      {:ok, conn.params}
    else
      _ -> {:error, :invalid_signature}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_webhook_secret do
    case webhook_secret() do
      nil -> :error
      secret -> {:ok, secret}
    end
  end

  defp parse_signature_header(header) do
    parts =
      header
      |> String.split(",")
      |> Map.new(fn part ->
        case String.split(part, "=", parts: 2) do
          [key, value] -> {key, value}
          [key] -> {key, nil}
        end
      end)

    case parts do
      %{"t" => t, "v1" => v1} -> {:ok, t, v1}
      _ -> :error
    end
  end

  defp sign(secret, timestamp, raw_body) do
    :hmac
    |> :crypto.mac(:sha256, secret, "#{timestamp}.#{raw_body}")
    |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
  end

  defp secret_key, do: Keyword.get(config(), :secret_key)
  defp webhook_secret, do: Keyword.get(config(), :webhook_secret)

  defp config, do: Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Public acquisition funnel (stories 848/849): the instant-quote
4	  calculator, capturing a lead's contact info once a price is shown,
5	  and quote acceptance — slot selection, cancellation-policy
6	  agreement, and Stripe card capture — that converts an accepted lead
7	  into a client + property + plan/job and issues portal access.
8	
9	  Orchestrates `CleanerCrm.Quoting` (rate-card pricing, via
10	  `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`), `CleanerCrm.Clients` (client +
11	  property), `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` (job/plan + slot availability),
12	  `CleanerCrm.Billing` (card capture via its `StripeGateway`), and
13	  `CleanerCrm.Portal` (the confirmation's magic-link).
14	
15	  Every function here is either scoped by an explicit `Scope`
16	  (mirroring every other context) or takes a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead`
17	  directly and resolves its own account scope from it — none of them
18	  are reachable from a logged-in user, so there's no caller `Scope` to
19	  receive from a plug.
20	
21	  ## Single-tenant storefront
22	
23	  `/book` carries no account identifier — no slug, no subdomain — so
24	  `public_scope/0` needs some other way to pick which account it prices
25	  against. It resolves, in order: the account with
26	  `CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account.storefront` set (an owner opts an
27	  account in from `/app/settings/booking`, via
28	  `CleanerCrm.Accounts.set_storefront/2`); otherwise the only account
29	  that exists, if there's exactly one; otherwise `nil` (see
30	  `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote`'s `unavailable` state).
31	
32	  Before the `storefront` flag existed (issue: three UAT accounts all
33	  named "Desert First Cleaning", the newest with a blank rate card),
34	  this resolved to the *most recently created* account unconditionally
35	  — any new signup creating a company silently stole the public `/book`
36	  storefront out from under the real one. A multi-tenant deployment
37	  still needs its own story to give each business a distinct public
38	  booking URL (e.g. `/book/:slug`) instead of one shared, opt-in
39	  storefront per deployment.
40	  """
41	
42	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
43	
44	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account
45	  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway
46	  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.{Lead, Notifier, Pricing}
47	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
48	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
49	  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
50	  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
51	  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard
52	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
53	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
54	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
55	
56	  # A reasonable number of visits to materialize up front for a
57	  # recurring booking, matching the office's own recurring-plan
58	  # builder default order of magnitude (see
59	  # `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent`) — the office can
60	  # always add more from the schedule board afterward.
61	  @default_occurrence_count 12
62	  @default_visit_duration_seconds 2 * 60 * 60
63	
64	  ## Public storefront
65	
66	  @doc "The (single-account MVP) scope every unauthenticated booking-funnel call resolves against."
67	  def public_scope, do: %Scope{active_account_id: resolve_public_account_id()}
68	
69	  @doc "The public rate card the instant-quote calculator prices against."
70	  def get_rate_card(%Scope{} = scope), do: Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)
71	
72	  defp resolve_public_account_id do
73	    case Repo.one(from a in Account, where: a.storefront == true, select: a.id, limit: 1) do
74	      nil -> resolve_single_account_id()
75	      account_id -> account_id
76	    end
77	  end
78	
79	  # No account has opted in as the storefront yet — fall back to "the"
80	  # account only when there's unambiguously just one (a fresh
81	  # deployment, or a test's own sandboxed transaction). Two or more
82	  # accounts with no flag set means there's no right answer, so `/book`
83	  # renders the `unavailable` state rather than guessing.
84	  defp resolve_single_account_id do
85	    case Repo.all(from a in Account, select: a.id, limit: 2) do
86	      [account_id] -> account_id
87	      _zero_or_many -> nil
88	    end
89	  end
90	
91	  ## Instant quote (calculator)
92	
93	  @doc """
94	  The calculator's live-preview changeset — never persisted, so the
95	  price can be computed before any contact info exists (see
96	  `quote_summary/2`).
97	  """
98	  def change_lead(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.quote_changeset(lead, attrs)
99	
100	  @doc "Everything `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` needs to render the live total."
101	  def quote_summary(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead),
102	    do: Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)
103	
104	  @doc """
105	  Captures a visitor's contact info against their computed price —
106	  locking in the quote as an accepted lead with its own acceptance
107	  token, the moment `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote`'s contact form is
108	  submitted. Always saved as `:accepted`: a lead is only ever persisted
109	  once contact info makes it one.
110	  """
111	  def create_lead(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
112	    %Lead{account_id: account_id}
113	    |> Lead.changeset(Map.merge(attrs, %{acceptance_token: generate_token(), status: :accepted}))
114	    |> Repo.insert()
115	  end
116	
117	  @doc "Looks up an accepted lead by its public acceptance-link token. No `Scope` — the token is the access control."
118	  def get_lead_by_token(token) when is_binary(token),
119	    do: Repo.get_by(Lead, acceptance_token: token)
120	
121	  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)
122	
123	  ## Acceptance: slot selection
124	
125	  def change_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.slot_changeset(lead, attrs)
126	
127	  @doc """
128	  Validates and applies a slot choice to the (still unpersisted) lead
129	  — rejected outright if the chosen date/time is already in the past
130	  (see `Lead.slot_changeset/3`). Nothing reaches the database here —
131	  `confirm_booking/3` is the only place a slot gets written, so
132	  availability (and, per issue 4e985412, whether the slot is still in
133	  the future) is always checked again right before a card is ever
134	  charged, no matter how long a client lingers on the
135	  cancellation-policy step. `now` defaults to the real clock but takes
136	  an override for tests.
137	  """
138	  def select_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
139	    with {:ok, %Lead{start_time: start_time} = slotted} <-
140	           lead |> Lead.slot_changeset(attrs, now) |> Ecto.Changeset.apply_action(:update) do
141	      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
142	    end
143	  end
144	
145	  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
146	    candidate = Time.add(start_time, @default_visit_duration_seconds, :second)
147	    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
148	  end
149	
150	  ## Acceptance: cancellation policy + payment
151	
152	  def change_confirmation(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}),
153	    do: Lead.confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs)
154	
155	  @doc "Whether the lead's selected slot is still free, account-wide (single-crew capacity, not per-cleaner)."
156	  def slot_available?(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: false
157	
158	  def slot_available?(%Lead{} = lead) do
159	    Scheduling.slot_available?(
160	      scope_for(lead),
161	      lead.scheduled_date,
162	      lead.start_time,
163	      lead.end_time
164	    )
165	  end
166	
167	  @doc """
168	  The confirmation step. Refuses without charging anything when the
169	  cancellation policy isn't agreed to, the selected slot has already
170	  passed, or the slot's been claimed by another booking since it was
171	  selected — otherwise submits the card and moves the lead to
172	  `:payment_pending`. Only the Stripe webhook
173	  (`receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever confirms or declines it from
174	  there, per the same webhook-confirms-everything rule
175	  `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for invoice payments.
176	
177	  The past-slot check (issue 4e985412) is defense in depth alongside
178	  `Lead.slot_changeset/3`'s own form-level validation: a slot picked
179	  as "later today" can go stale by the time the client actually
180	  submits payment, the same reason `slot_available?/1` is re-checked
181	  here rather than trusted from selection time. `now` defaults to the
182	  real clock but takes an override for tests.
183	  """
184	  def confirm_booking(lead, params, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())
185	
186	  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, %{"payment_method" => payment_method} = params, now) do
187	    cond do
188	      Map.get(params, "policy_agreed") not in [true, "true"] ->
189	        {:error, :policy_required}
190	
191	      not Lead.slot_in_future?(lead, now) ->
192	        {:error, :slot_in_past}
193	
194	      not slot_available?(lead) ->
195	        {:error, :slot_unavailable}
196	
197	      true ->
198	        submit_payment(lead, payment_method)
199	    end
200	  end
201	
202	  defp submit_payment(%Lead{} = lead, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
203	    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
204	           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
205	             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
206	             payment_method: payment_method,
207	             off_session: false,
208	             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
209	           }) do
210	      lead
211	      |> Lead.changeset(%{
212	        policy_agreed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
213	        status: :payment_pending,
214	        stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id
215	      })
216	      # `select_slot/2` never touches the database (see its doc) — the
217	      # slot lives only on this in-memory `lead` struct until now, so
218	      # `cast/3` (which diffs against the struct's own field, not the
219	      # row) would otherwise see "no change" and silently leave the
220	      # database's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time at `nil`.
221	      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:scheduled_date, lead.scheduled_date)
222	      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:start_time, lead.start_time)
223	      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:end_time, lead.end_time)
224	      |> Repo.update()
225	    end
226	  end
227	
228	  ## Webhook
229	
230	  @doc """
231	  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request for a
232	  booking's payment — `CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController` falls
233	  back to this once `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1` reports the
234	  event isn't one of its own invoices.
235	  """
236	  def receive_payment_webhook(conn) do
237	    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
238	      apply_webhook_event(event)
239	    end
240	  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking do
  @moduledoc """
  Public acquisition funnel (stories 848/849): the instant-quote
  calculator, capturing a lead's contact info once a price is shown,
  and quote acceptance — slot selection, cancellation-policy
  agreement, and Stripe card capture — that converts an accepted lead
  into a client + property + plan/job and issues portal access.

  Orchestrates `CleanerCrm.Quoting` (rate-card pricing, via
  `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`), `CleanerCrm.Clients` (client +
  property), `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` (job/plan + slot availability),
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` (card capture via its `StripeGateway`), and
  `CleanerCrm.Portal` (the confirmation's magic-link).

  Every function here is either scoped by an explicit `Scope`
  (mirroring every other context) or takes a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead`
  directly and resolves its own account scope from it — none of them
  are reachable from a logged-in user, so there's no caller `Scope` to
  receive from a plug.

  ## Single-tenant storefront

  `/book` carries no account identifier — no slug, no subdomain — so
  `public_scope/0` needs some other way to pick which account it prices
  against. It resolves, in order: the account with
  `CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account.storefront` set (an owner opts an
  account in from `/app/settings/booking`, via
  `CleanerCrm.Accounts.set_storefront/2`); otherwise the only account
  that exists, if there's exactly one; otherwise `nil` (see
  `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote`'s `unavailable` state).

  Before the `storefront` flag existed (issue: three UAT accounts all
  named "Desert First Cleaning", the newest with a blank rate card),
  this resolved to the *most recently created* account unconditionally
  — any new signup creating a company silently stole the public `/book`
  storefront out from under the real one. A multi-tenant deployment
  still needs its own story to give each business a distinct public
  booking URL (e.g. `/book/:slug`) instead of one shared, opt-in
  storefront per deployment.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.{Lead, Notifier, Pricing}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # A reasonable number of visits to materialize up front for a
  # recurring booking, matching the office's own recurring-plan
  # builder default order of magnitude (see
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent`) — the office can
  # always add more from the schedule board afterward.
  @default_occurrence_count 12
  @default_visit_duration_seconds 2 * 60 * 60

  ## Public storefront

  @doc "The (single-account MVP) scope every unauthenticated booking-funnel call resolves against."
  def public_scope, do: %Scope{active_account_id: resolve_public_account_id()}

  @doc "The public rate card the instant-quote calculator prices against."
  def get_rate_card(%Scope{} = scope), do: Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)

  defp resolve_public_account_id do
    case Repo.one(from a in Account, where: a.storefront == true, select: a.id, limit: 1) do
      nil -> resolve_single_account_id()
      account_id -> account_id
    end
  end

  # No account has opted in as the storefront yet — fall back to "the"
  # account only when there's unambiguously just one (a fresh
  # deployment, or a test's own sandboxed transaction). Two or more
  # accounts with no flag set means there's no right answer, so `/book`
  # renders the `unavailable` state rather than guessing.
  defp resolve_single_account_id do
    case Repo.all(from a in Account, select: a.id, limit: 2) do
      [account_id] -> account_id
      _zero_or_many -> nil
    end
  end

  ## Instant quote (calculator)

  @doc """
  The calculator's live-preview changeset — never persisted, so the
  price can be computed before any contact info exists (see
  `quote_summary/2`).
  """
  def change_lead(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.quote_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc "Everything `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` needs to render the live total."
  def quote_summary(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead),
    do: Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)

  @doc """
  Captures a visitor's contact info against their computed price —
  locking in the quote as an accepted lead with its own acceptance
  token, the moment `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote`'s contact form is
  submitted. Always saved as `:accepted`: a lead is only ever persisted
  once contact info makes it one.
  """
  def create_lead(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Lead{account_id: account_id}
    |> Lead.changeset(Map.merge(attrs, %{acceptance_token: generate_token(), status: :accepted}))
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "Looks up an accepted lead by its public acceptance-link token. No `Scope` — the token is the access control."
  def get_lead_by_token(token) when is_binary(token),
    do: Repo.get_by(Lead, acceptance_token: token)

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  ## Acceptance: slot selection

  def change_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.slot_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc """
  Validates and applies a slot choice to the (still unpersisted) lead
  — rejected outright if the chosen date/time is already in the past
  (see `Lead.slot_changeset/3`). Nothing reaches the database here —
  `confirm_booking/3` is the only place a slot gets written, so
  availability (and, per issue 4e985412, whether the slot is still in
  the future) is always checked again right before a card is ever
  charged, no matter how long a client lingers on the
  cancellation-policy step. `now` defaults to the real clock but takes
  an override for tests.
  """
  def select_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    with {:ok, %Lead{start_time: start_time} = slotted} <-
           lead |> Lead.slot_changeset(attrs, now) |> Ecto.Changeset.apply_action(:update) do
      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
    end
  end

  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, @default_visit_duration_seconds, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  ## Acceptance: cancellation policy + payment

  def change_confirmation(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}),
    do: Lead.confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc "Whether the lead's selected slot is still free, account-wide (single-crew capacity, not per-cleaner)."
  def slot_available?(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: false

  def slot_available?(%Lead{} = lead) do
    Scheduling.slot_available?(
      scope_for(lead),
      lead.scheduled_date,
      lead.start_time,
      lead.end_time
    )
  end

  @doc """
  The confirmation step. Refuses without charging anything when the
  cancellation policy isn't agreed to, the selected slot has already
  passed, or the slot's been claimed by another booking since it was
  selected — otherwise submits the card and moves the lead to
  `:payment_pending`. Only the Stripe webhook
  (`receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever confirms or declines it from
  there, per the same webhook-confirms-everything rule
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for invoice payments.

  The past-slot check (issue 4e985412) is defense in depth alongside
  `Lead.slot_changeset/3`'s own form-level validation: a slot picked
  as "later today" can go stale by the time the client actually
  submits payment, the same reason `slot_available?/1` is re-checked
  here rather than trusted from selection time. `now` defaults to the
  real clock but takes an override for tests.
  """
  def confirm_booking(lead, params, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())

  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, %{"payment_method" => payment_method} = params, now) do
    cond do
      Map.get(params, "policy_agreed") not in [true, "true"] ->
        {:error, :policy_required}

      not Lead.slot_in_future?(lead, now) ->
        {:error, :slot_in_past}

      not slot_available?(lead) ->
        {:error, :slot_unavailable}

      true ->
        submit_payment(lead, payment_method)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(%Lead{} = lead, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
             payment_method: payment_method,
             off_session: false,
             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
           }) do
      lead
      |> Lead.changeset(%{
        policy_agreed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
        status: :payment_pending,
        stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id
      })
      # `select_slot/2` never touches the database (see its doc) — the
      # slot lives only on this in-memory `lead` struct until now, so
      # `cast/3` (which diffs against the struct's own field, not the
      # row) would otherwise see "no change" and silently leave the
      # database's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time at `nil`.
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:scheduled_date, lead.scheduled_date)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:start_time, lead.start_time)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:end_time, lead.end_time)
      |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request for a
  booking's payment — `CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController` falls
  back to this once `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1` reports the
  event isn't one of its own invoices.
  """
  def receive_payment_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      convert_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      decline_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:error, :lead_not_found}

  defp find_lead_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"lead_id" => lead_id}} when is_binary(lead_id) -> fetch_lead(lead_id)
      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) -> fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id)
      _ -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead(lead_id) do
    case Repo.get(Lead, lead_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Lead, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp decline_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    lead |> Lead.changeset(%{status: :payment_declined}) |> Repo.update()
  end

  # Idempotent against a redelivered webhook — Stripe (and its Test
  # stand-in) offers no stronger delivery guarantee than at-least-once.
  defp convert_lead(%Lead{status: :converted} = lead), do: {:ok, lead}

  defp convert_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    scope = scope_for(lead)

    with {:ok, {updated, client}} <-
           Repo.transact(fn ->
             with {:ok, client} <- Clients.create_client(scope, client_attrs(lead)),
                  {:ok, property} <- Clients.create_property(scope, property_attrs(client)),
                  {:ok, visit_ids} <- schedule_visit(scope, lead, property),
                  {:ok, updated} <- finalize_conversion(lead, client, property, visit_ids) do
               {:ok, {updated, client}}
             end
           end) do
      issue_portal_access(updated, client)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp client_attrs(%Lead{} = lead) do
    %{
      name: lead.client_name,
      email: lead.client_email,
      phone: lead.client_phone,
      card_on_file: true
    }
  end

  # No property inputs exist anywhere in the public funnel (story 848's
  # form only ever asks for what prices the job) — the office fills
  # the real address in from the client record afterward. Named after
  # the client rather than a generic placeholder so the schedule board
  # (which shows a job's property, never its client, on the card) still
  # identifies whose visit this is until that happens.
  defp property_attrs(%Client{} = client) do
    %{client_id: client.id, service_address: "#{client.name} — address to be confirmed"}
  end

  defp schedule_visit(scope, %Lead{frequency: :one_time} = lead, property) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
             property_id: property.id,
             scheduled_date: lead.scheduled_date,
             start_time: lead.start_time,
             end_time: lead.end_time,
             agreed_price_cents: lead.total_cents,
             status: :scheduled
           }) do
      {:ok, %{job_id: job.id, recurring_plan_id: nil}}
    end
  end

  defp schedule_visit(scope, %Lead{} = lead, property) do
    with {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} <-
           Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(scope, %{
             property_id: property.id,
             recurrence: lead.frequency,
             start_date: lead.scheduled_date,
             occurrence_count: @default_occurrence_count,
             start_time: lead.start_time,
             end_time: lead.end_time,
             agreed_price_cents: lead.total_cents
           }) do
      {:ok, %{job_id: nil, recurring_plan_id: plan.id}}
    end
  end

  defp finalize_conversion(%Lead{} = lead, %Client{} = client, property, visit_ids) do
    lead
    |> Lead.changeset(
      Map.merge(%{status: :converted, client_id: client.id, property_id: property.id}, visit_ids)
    )
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp issue_portal_access(%Lead{} = lead, %Client{} = client) do
    with {:ok, session} <- Portal.create_portal_session(client, %{}) do
      Notifier.deliver_confirmation(lead, portal_url(session))
    end
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp portal_url(session), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/portal/access/#{session.token}"

  defp scope_for(%Lead{account_id: account_id}), do: %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}
end

import Config

# config/runtime.exs is executed for all environments, including
# during releases. It is executed after compilation and before the
# system starts, so it is typically used to load production configuration
# and secrets from environment variables or elsewhere. Do not define
# any compile-time configuration in here, as it won't be applied.
# The block below contains prod specific runtime configuration.

# ## Using releases
#
# If you use `mix release`, you need to explicitly enable the server
# by passing the PHX_SERVER=true when you start it:
#
#     PHX_SERVER=true bin/cleaner_crm start
#
# Alternatively, you can use `mix phx.gen.release` to generate a `bin/server`
# script that automatically sets the env var above.
if System.get_env("PHX_SERVER") do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint, server: true
end

# === Secret loading ==========================================================
#
# Deployed containers (UAT + prod, both MIX_ENV=prod) carry only AWS
# bootstrap creds + APP_ENV; every app secret is fetched from SSM
# Parameter Store (/cleaner_crm/<APP_ENV>/*) into System env here,
# BEFORE any config below reads it. Local dev/test never set APP_ENV.
if config_env() == :prod do
  case System.get_env("APP_ENV") do
    nil -> :ok
    app_env -> CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!(app_env)
  end
end

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [port: String.to_integer(System.get_env("PORT", "4100"))]

# CodeMySpec feedback widget / OAuth provider credentials.
# Generate the client ID/secret on the CodeMySpec project page and set them
# as env vars before deploying.
config :cleaner_crm,
  codemyspec_url: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_URL") || "https://codemyspec.com",
  codemyspec_client_id: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_ID"),
  codemyspec_client_secret: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_SECRET")

# Stripe credentials — see .code_my_spec/integrations/stripe.md. Only
# CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live (never the test adapter) reads these.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
  secret_key: System.get_env("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"),
  webhook_secret: System.get_env("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET")

# STRIPE_ADAPTER=test swaps in the no-network fake gateway — for UAT
# until real Stripe test keys are seeded. Anything else keeps the
# compile-time default (Live in prod, Test in dev — see config files).
if System.get_env("STRIPE_ADAPTER") == "test" do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
    adapter: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Test
end

# Twilio — SMS delivery per the sms-delivery ADR. Unconditional (like
# the Stripe block above), not `:prod`-only: `CleanerCrm.Notifications.
# Delivery.Twilio` must always have *some* config to read. Missing
# credentials in dev/CI aren't an error here — `Twilio.send_sms/2`
# returns `{:error, :not_configured}` and the caller falls back to
# email, it never reaches the network or raises.
twilio_host = System.get_env("PHX_HOST") || "localhost:4100"

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio,
  account_sid: System.get_env("TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID"),

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.AcceptTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 4e985412: the `/book/accept/:token` slot-selection form
  accepted any date, including years in the past, with zero
  validation — QA drove `scheduled_date=2020-01-01` through card
  capture and it converted into a real scheduled job. No spex/BDD
  story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead. See also
  `CleanerCrm.BookingTest` for the context-level (`Booking`/`Lead`)
  coverage, including the defense-in-depth re-check at confirmation.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      Booking.create_lead(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  test "a past scheduled date is rejected with a clear error and never reaches the confirm step",
       %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    lead = lead_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

    html =
      accept_live
      |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
        booking: %{scheduled_date: "2020-01-01", start_time: "09:00"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

    assert html =~ "must be today or later"
    assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='slot-form']")
    refute has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='confirmation-form']")

    reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
    assert reloaded.scheduled_date == nil
  end

  test "a valid future date advances to the confirmation step", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    lead = lead_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

    accept_live
    |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
      booking: %{
        scheduled_date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
        start_time: "09:00"
      }
    )
    |> render_submit()

    assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='confirmation-form']")
  end
end

=== criterion_7233_client_enters_a_valid_card_and_the_booking_confirms_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7233Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7233 — Client enters a valid card and the booking
  confirms: once the payment gateway accepts the card, it is stored
  on file and the booking is confirmed.

  As with story 836's card charges, the gateway's acceptance is only
  final once the provider confirms it via `POST /webhooks/stripe`
  (see `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1`) — submitting the card
  moves the booking to a pending-payment state; this spec's subject
  is the transition that follows the provider's confirmation.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the payment gateway accepting the card confirms the booking" do
    scenario "client enters a valid card and the booking confirms" do
      given_ "the client has agreed to the cancellation policy", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead = Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{total_cents: 19_500})

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, accept_live: accept_live})}
      end

      when_ "the client enters a valid card and the payment gateway accepts it", context do
        context.accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
          booking: %{policy_agreed: "true", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        assert has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='payment-pending']")

        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => "pi_test_booking_succeeded",
              "metadata" => %{"lead_id" => to_string(context.lead.id)}
            }
          }
        }

        response =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
          |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
          |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :webhook_response, response)}
      end

      then_ "the card is stored on file and the booking is confirmed", context do
        {:ok, accept_live, _html} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{context.lead.acceptance_token}")

        assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='booking-confirmed']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7234Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7234 — Payment gateway declines the card: the booking is
  not confirmed and the client is prompted to retry with a different
  card.

  Mirrors story 836's decline handling: the provider's decline
  arrives via `POST /webhooks/stripe` (`payment_intent.payment_failed`),
  never as a synchronous response to submitting the card.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the payment gateway declining the card leaves the booking unconfirmed" do
    scenario "payment gateway declines the card" do
      given_ "the client has agreed to the cancellation policy and submitted a card", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead = Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{total_cents: 19_500})

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
          booking: %{policy_agreed: "true", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='payment-pending']")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, accept_live: accept_live})}
      end

      when_ "the payment gateway declines the card", context do
        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => "pi_test_booking_declined",
              "metadata" => %{"lead_id" => to_string(context.lead.id)}
            }
          }
        }

        response =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
          |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
          |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :webhook_response, response)}
      end

      then_ "the booking is not confirmed and the client is prompted to retry with a different card",
            context do
        {:ok, accept_live, _html} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{context.lead.acceptance_token}")

        assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='payment-declined-message']")
        refute has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='booking-confirmed']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7236Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7236 — Confirmed booking appears for client and business
  with portal access: confirming converts the accepted quote into a
  scheduled job visible to both sides, and the client receives a
  confirmation containing a magic-link to their portal.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "confirming the booking makes the visit visible to both sides and grants portal access" do
    scenario "confirmed booking appears for client and business with portal access" do
      given_ "the booking has been confirmed with card on file", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead =
          Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{
            total_cents: 19_500,
            client_name: "Dana Prescott",
            client_email: "dana@example.com"
          })

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
          booking: %{policy_agreed: "true", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => "pi_test_booking_confirmed",
              "metadata" => %{"lead_id" => to_string(lead.id)}
            }
          }
        }

        Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
        |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
        |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
        |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, account: account, owner_conn: owner_conn})}
      end

      when_ "the confirmation completes", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the visit appears as scheduled for both the business and the client, and the client receives a confirmation containing a magic-link to their portal",
            context do
        {:ok, accept_live, _html} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{context.lead.acceptance_token}")

        assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='booking-confirmed']")

        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/app/schedule")
        assert render(board_live) =~ context.lead.client_name

        assert_email_sent(fn email ->
          email.to == [{"", context.lead.client_email}] and
            email.html_body =~ ~r{href="[^"]*portal[^"]*"}i
        end)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.BookingTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 4e985412: `/book/accept/:token`'s slot-selection form
  accepted any date — including years in the past — with zero
  validation, and QA drove a `scheduled_date` of 2020-01-01 all the
  way through card capture into a real scheduled job. Both guards
  added for it are exercised here:

    * `Lead.slot_changeset/3` (via `Booking.select_slot/3`) — the
      form-level guard, rejecting a past date/time outright.
    * `Booking.confirm_booking/3` — the defense-in-depth re-check
      right before a card is charged, in case a slot that was future
      at selection time goes stale (or a lead's slot fields were set
      some other way) by the time the client actually submits payment.

  No spex/BDD story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead,
  mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.TemplatesTest`'s precedent for
  issue-only coverage.

  Also covers the live UAT regression where `public_scope/0` resolved
  the *newest* account unconditionally: three UAT accounts named
  "Desert First Cleaning" existed, and the newest — with a blank rate
  card — silently became the `/book` storefront. `describe
  "public_scope/0"` below drives the fix (the `storefront` flag, with
  an exactly-one-account fallback and `nil` otherwise) directly.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      Booking.create_lead(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  describe "select_slot/3" do
    test "rejects a scheduled_date years in the past" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => "2020-01-01",
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert "must be today or later" in errors_on(changeset).scheduled_date
    end

    test "rejects today's date once the chosen start time has already passed" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      today = Date.utc_today()
      now = DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(
                 lead,
                 %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
                 now
               )

      assert "must be later than the current time" in errors_on(changeset).start_time
    end

    test "accepts a future date" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      future_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)

      assert {:ok, slotted} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(future_date),
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert slotted.scheduled_date == future_date
    end
  end

  describe "confirm_booking/3 (defense in depth against a past slot)" do
    test "refuses a lead whose slot fields are already in the past, without charging a card" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      past_lead = %{lead | scheduled_date: ~D[2020-01-01], start_time: ~T[09:00:00]}

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(past_lead, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
      assert reloaded.status == :accepted
      assert reloaded.stripe_payment_intent_id == nil
    end

    test "refuses a slot picked for later today once that time has passed by confirmation" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      today = Date.utc_today()

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(
          lead,
          %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
          DateTime.new!(today, ~T[13:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
        )

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(
                 slotted,
                 %{"policy_agreed" => "true", "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"},
                 DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
               )
    end

    test "still confirms and moves the lead to payment_pending for a genuinely future slot" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
          "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
          "start_time" => "09:00"
        })

      assert {:ok, updated} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(slotted, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      assert updated.status == :payment_pending
    end
  end

  describe "public_scope/0" do
    test "resolves nil when no account exists at all" do
      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == nil
    end

    test "resolves the only account when exactly one exists and none is flagged" do
      scope = scope_fixture()

      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == scope.active_account_id
    end

    test "resolves nil when multiple accounts exist and none is flagged as the storefront" do
      scope_fixture()
      scope_fixture()

      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == nil
    end

    test "resolves the storefront-flagged account even though a newer account exists" do
      older = scope_fixture()
      {:ok, _updated} = Accounts.set_storefront(older, true)
      _newer = scope_fixture()

      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == older.active_account_id
    end

    test "moving the storefront flag to a different account changes which one resolves" do
      first = scope_fixture()
      second = scope_fixture()

      {:ok, _} = Accounts.set_storefront(first, true)
      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == first.active_account_id

      {:ok, _} = Accounts.set_storefront(second, true)
      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == second.active_account_id

      reloaded_first = Accounts.get_account!(first, first.active_account_id)
      refute reloaded_first.storefront
    end

    test "only an owner may set the storefront flag" do
      owner_scope = scope_fixture()
      admin_user = user_fixture()

      {:ok, _member} =
        Accounts.add_user_to_account(
          owner_scope,
          admin_user.id,
          owner_scope.active_account_id,
          :admin
        )

      admin_scope = %{
        Scope.for_user(admin_user)
        | active_account_id: owner_scope.active_account_id
      }

      assert_raise RuntimeError, ~r/Unauthorized/, fn ->
        Accounts.set_storefront(admin_scope, true)
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGatewayTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Guards the Live adapter's graceful-degradation behavior: a deploy
  missing `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (any dev machine,
  by design — see `config/dev.exs`) must get `{:error, _}` back from
  every call, never a raised exception that would crash the calling
  LiveView or turn a public controller response into a raw 500.
  """

  use ExUnit.Case, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live

  setup do
    original = Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])

    on_exit(fn ->
      Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, original)
    end)

    Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])
    :ok
  end

  describe "create_payment_intent/1 with no STRIPE_SECRET_KEY configured" do
    test "returns an error tuple instead of raising" do
      assert {:error, %{"code" => "not_configured"}} =
               Live.create_payment_intent(%{amount_cents: 15_000, payment_method: "pm_card_visa"})
    end
  end

  describe "verify_webhook_event/1 with no STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET configured" do
    test "returns an error tuple instead of raising, even with a signature header" do
      conn =
        Plug.Test.conn(:post, "/webhooks/stripe", %{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"})
        |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("stripe-signature", "t=123,v1=deadbeef")
        |> Plug.Conn.assign(:raw_body, ~s({"type":"payment_intent.succeeded"}))

      assert {:error, :invalid_signature} = Live.verify_webhook_event(conn)
    end

    test "returns an error tuple when there's no signature header at all" do
      conn = Plug.Test.conn(:post, "/webhooks/stripe", %{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"})

      assert {:error, :invalid_signature} = Live.verify_webhook_event(conn)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FeedbackWidget do
  @moduledoc """
  Floating feedback widget for reporting issues to CodeMySpec.

  Self-contained LiveComponent that checks its own connection status.
  Renders nothing if the user hasn't connected to CodeMySpec.
  No hooks, no prop-drilling, no layout attr changes needed.

  ## Usage

  Add to Layouts.app (current_scope is already passed):

      <.live_component
        module={CleanerCrmWeb.FeedbackWidget}
        id="codemyspec-feedback"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
      />
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component

  alias CleanerCrm.Codemyspec.Client

  @impl true
  def update(assigns, socket) do
    socket = assign(socket, assigns)

    socket =
      if connected?(socket) && !Map.has_key?(socket.assigns, :connected) do
        connected =
          case socket.assigns[:current_scope] do
            nil -> false
            scope -> Client.connected?(scope)
          end

        socket
        |> assign(:connected, connected)
        |> assign(:expanded, false)
        |> assign(:submitted, false)
        |> assign(:error, nil)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live do
  @moduledoc """
  Talks to the real Stripe API over `Req` and verifies webhook
  signatures per Stripe's documented scheme (HMAC-SHA256 over
  `"{timestamp}.{raw body}"`, compared against the `Stripe-Signature`
  header).

  Requires `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (see
  `.code_my_spec/integrations/stripe.md`). Verifying the signature
  needs the exact raw request bytes, which normal body parsing
  discards — `CleanerCrmWeb.CacheBodyReader` stashes them into
  `conn.assigns[:raw_body]` for the webhook route specifically.

  Missing credentials are a recoverable operational condition, not a
  bug: `create_payment_intent/1` returns `{:error, %{"code" =>
  "not_configured", ...}}` and `verify_webhook_event/1` returns
  `{:error, :invalid_signature}` rather than raising, so a deploy
  without keys degrades to a friendly error for the caller instead of
  crashing the LiveView or returning a raw 500 from the public
  `/pay/:token` or `/webhooks/stripe` endpoints. `config/dev.exs`
  avoids this entirely by defaulting to `StripeGateway.Test` — dev
  machines don't carry these secrets.
  """

  @behaviour CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway

  @base_url "https://api.stripe.com/v1"

  @impl true
  def create_payment_intent(
        %{amount_cents: amount_cents, payment_method: payment_method} = params
      ) do
    with {:ok, key} <- fetch_secret_key() do
      body =
        %{
          "amount" => amount_cents,
          "currency" => "usd",
          "payment_method" => payment_method,
          "confirm" => true,
          "off_session" => Map.get(params, :off_session, false),
          # Card-only, no redirect-based methods: confirming
          # server-side without a return_url requires redirects off.
          "automatic_payment_methods[enabled]" => true,
          "automatic_payment_methods[allow_redirects]" => "never"
        }
        |> put_metadata(Map.get(params, :metadata, %{}))

      @base_url
      |> Kernel.<>("/payment_intents")
      |> Req.post(form: body, auth: {:bearer, key})
      |> handle_response()
    end
  end

  # A misconfigured deploy (secret unset) is a recoverable operational
  # condition here, not a bug — callers already handle `{:error, _}` by
  # showing the payer/owner a friendly message, so this must never raise.
  defp fetch_secret_key do
    case secret_key() do
      nil ->
        {:error,
         %{"code" => "not_configured", "message" => "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not configured"}}

      key ->
        {:ok, key}
    end
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{status: status, body: %{"id" => id, "status" => stripe_status}}})
       when status in 200..299 do
    {:ok, %{id: id, status: stripe_status}}
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{body: %{"error" => error}}}), do: {:error, error}

  defp handle_response({:error, reason}),
    do: {:error, %{"code" => "request_failed", "message" => inspect(reason)}}

  defp put_metadata(body, metadata) do
    Enum.reduce(metadata, body, fn {key, value}, acc ->
      Map.put(acc, "metadata[#{key}]", to_string(value))
    end)
  end

  @impl true
  def verify_webhook_event(conn) do
    with {:ok, secret} <- fetch_webhook_secret(),
         [signature_header] <- Plug.Conn.get_req_header(conn, "stripe-signature"),
         raw_body when is_binary(raw_body) <- conn.assigns[:raw_body],
         {:ok, timestamp, expected_signature} <- parse_signature_header(signature_header),
         true <- Plug.Crypto.secure_compare(sign(secret, timestamp, raw_body), expected_signature) do
      {:ok, conn.params}
    else
      _ -> {:error, :invalid_signature}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_webhook_secret do
    case webhook_secret() do
      nil -> :error
      secret -> {:ok, secret}
    end
  end

  defp parse_signature_header(header) do
    parts =
      header
      |> String.split(",")
      |> Map.new(fn part ->
        case String.split(part, "=", parts: 2) do
          [key, value] -> {key, value}
          [key] -> {key, nil}
        end
      end)

    case parts do
      %{"t" => t, "v1" => v1} -> {:ok, t, v1}
      _ -> :error
    end
  end

  defp sign(secret, timestamp, raw_body) do
    :hmac
    |> :crypto.mac(:sha256, secret, "#{timestamp}.#{raw_body}")
    |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
  end

  defp secret_key, do: Keyword.get(config(), :secret_key)
  defp webhook_secret, do: Keyword.get(config(), :webhook_secret)

  defp config, do: Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])
end

@doc """
  The confirmation step. Refuses without charging anything when the
  cancellation policy isn't agreed to, the selected slot has already
  passed, or the slot's been claimed by another booking since it was
  selected — otherwise moves the lead to `:payment_pending` and
  submits the card. Only the Stripe webhook
  (`receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever confirms or declines it from
  there, per the same webhook-confirms-everything rule
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for invoice payments.

  Two shapes of `params` reach this function, depending on whether
  `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Accept` has a Stripe publishable key
  configured (see `config/runtime.exs`):

    * `"payment_method"` present — the dev/test fallback (a hidden
      `pm_card_visa` field until real keys exist anywhere but UAT):
      the intent is confirmed synchronously and this returns
      `{:ok, %Lead{}}`, exactly as before.
    * `"payment_method"` absent — the Stripe Elements flow: the intent
      is created *unconfirmed* so the client can finish it in the
      browser with its own `client_secret`, returned here as
      `{:ok, %{lead: %Lead{}, client_secret: String.t()}}` for the
      LiveView to mount the Payment Element.

  The past-slot check (issue 4e985412) is defense in depth alongside
  `Lead.slot_changeset/3`'s own form-level validation: a slot picked
  as "later today" can go stale by the time the client actually
  submits payment, the same reason `slot_available?/1` is re-checked
  here rather than trusted from selection time. `now` defaults to the
  real clock but takes an override for tests.
  """
  def confirm_booking(lead, params, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())

  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, %{"payment_method" => payment_method} = params, now) do
    with :ok <- validate_confirmation(lead, params, now) do
      submit_payment(lead, payment_method)
    end
  end

  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, params, now) do
    with :ok <- validate_confirmation(lead, params, now) do
      submit_unconfirmed_payment(lead)
    end
  end

  defp validate_confirmation(lead, params, now) do
    cond do
      Map.get(params, "policy_agreed") not in [true, "true"] -> {:error, :policy_required}
      not Lead.slot_in_future?(lead, now) -> {:error, :slot_in_past}
      not slot_available?(lead) -> {:error, :slot_unavailable}
      true -> :ok
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(%Lead{} = lead, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
             payment_method: payment_method,
             off_session: false,
             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
           }) do
      mark_payment_pending(lead, intent_id)
    end
  end

  # Stripe Elements flow: no payment method yet, so no `confirm` — the
  # client finishes this intent in the browser (see the
  # ".StripePaymentElement" hook in `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Accept`)
  # using the `client_secret` handed back here.
  defp submit_unconfirmed_payment(%Lead{} = lead) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id, client_secret: client_secret}} <-
           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
             confirm: false,
             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
           }),
         {:ok, updated} <- mark_payment_pending(lead, intent_id) do
      {:ok, %{lead: updated, client_secret: client_secret}}
    end
  end

  defp mark_payment_pending(%Lead{} = lead, intent_id) do
    lead
    |> Lead.changeset(%{
      policy_agreed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      status: :payment_pending,
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id
    })
    # `select_slot/2` never touches the database (see its doc) — the
    # slot lives only on this in-memory `lead` struct until now, so
    # `cast/3` (which diffs against the struct's own field, not the
    # row) would otherwise see "no change" and silently leave the
    # database's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time at `nil`.
    |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:scheduled_date, lead.scheduled_date)
    |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:start_time, lead.start_time)
    |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:end_time, lead.end_time)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

import Config

# config/runtime.exs is executed for all environments, including
# during releases. It is executed after compilation and before the
# system starts, so it is typically used to load production configuration
# and secrets from environment variables or elsewhere. Do not define
# any compile-time configuration in here, as it won't be applied.
# The block below contains prod specific runtime configuration.

# ## Using releases
#
# If you use `mix release`, you need to explicitly enable the server
# by passing the PHX_SERVER=true when you start it:
#
#     PHX_SERVER=true bin/cleaner_crm start
#
# Alternatively, you can use `mix phx.gen.release` to generate a `bin/server`
# script that automatically sets the env var above.
if System.get_env("PHX_SERVER") do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint, server: true
end

# === Secret loading ==========================================================
#
# Deployed containers (UAT + prod, both MIX_ENV=prod) carry only AWS
# bootstrap creds + APP_ENV; every app secret is fetched from SSM
# Parameter Store (/cleaner_crm/<APP_ENV>/*) into System env here,
# BEFORE any config below reads it. Local dev/test never set APP_ENV.
if config_env() == :prod do
  case System.get_env("APP_ENV") do
    nil -> :ok
    app_env -> CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!(app_env)
  end
end

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [port: String.to_integer(System.get_env("PORT", "4100"))]

# CodeMySpec feedback widget / OAuth provider credentials.
# Generate the client ID/secret on the CodeMySpec project page and set them
# as env vars before deploying.
config :cleaner_crm,
  codemyspec_url: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_URL") || "https://codemyspec.com",
  codemyspec_client_id: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_ID"),
  codemyspec_client_secret: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_SECRET")

# Stripe credentials — see .code_my_spec/integrations/stripe.md. Only
# CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live (never the test adapter) reads these.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
  secret_key: System.get_env("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"),
  webhook_secret: System.get_env("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET")

# STRIPE_ADAPTER=test swaps in the no-network fake gateway — for UAT
# until real Stripe test keys are seeded. Anything else keeps the
# compile-time default (Live in prod, Test in dev — see config files).
if System.get_env("STRIPE_ADAPTER") == "test" do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
    adapter: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Test
end

# Twilio — SMS delivery per the sms-delivery ADR. Unconditional (like
# the Stripe block above), not `:prod`-only: `CleanerCrm.Notifications.
# Delivery.Twilio` must always have *some* config to read. Missing
# credentials in dev/CI aren't an error here — `Twilio.send_sms/2`
# returns `{:error, :not_configured}` and the caller falls back to
# email, it never reaches the network or raises.
twilio_host = System.get_env("PHX_HOST") || "localhost:4100"

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio,
  account_sid: System.get_env("TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID"),
  auth_token: System.get_env("TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN"),
  from_number: System.get_env("TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER"),
  status_callback_url: "https://#{twilio_host}/webhooks/twilio"

if config_env() == :prod do
  # Encrypted-token vault key — required in production.
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Vault,
    ciphers: [
      default:
        {Cloak.Ciphers.AES.GCM,
         tag: "AES.GCM.V1",
         key:
           Base.decode64!(
             System.get_env("CLOAK_KEY") ||
               raise("environment variable CLOAK_KEY is missing (base64 32-byte key)")
           )}
    ]
end

if config_env() == :prod do
  database_url =
    System.get_env("DATABASE_URL") ||
      raise """
      environment variable DATABASE_URL is missing.
      For example: ecto://USER:PASS@HOST/DATABASE
      """

  maybe_ipv6 = if System.get_env("ECTO_IPV6") in ~w(true 1), do: [:inet6], else: []

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
    # ssl: true,
    url: database_url,
    pool_size: String.to_integer(System.get_env("POOL_SIZE") || "10"),
    # For machines with several cores, consider starting multiple pools of `pool_size`
    # pool_count: 4,
    socket_options: maybe_ipv6

  # The secret key base is used to sign/encrypt cookies and other secrets.
  # A default value is used in config/dev.exs and config/test.exs but you
  # want to use a different value for prod and you most likely don't want
  # to check this value into version control, so we use an environment
  # variable instead.
  secret_key_base =
    System.get_env("SECRET_KEY_BASE") ||
      raise """
      environment variable SECRET_KEY_BASE is missing.
      You can generate one by calling: mix phx.gen.secret
      """

  host = System.get_env("PHX_HOST") || "example.com"

  config :cleaner_crm, :dns_cluster_query, System.get_env("DNS_CLUSTER_QUERY")

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
    url: [host: host, port: 443, scheme: "https"],
    http: [
      # Enable IPv6 and bind on all interfaces.
      # Set it to  {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1} for local network only access.
      # See the documentation on https://bandit.hexdocs.pm/Bandit.html#t:options/0
      # for details about using IPv6 vs IPv4 and loopback vs public addresses.
      ip: {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
    ],
    secret_key_base: secret_key_base

  # Resend for real email delivery (fleet ADR). Only when the key is
  # present — a UAT/prod box without it keeps the Local adapter and
  # boots fine, emails just stay undelivered.
  if resend_api_key = System.get_env("RESEND_API_KEY") do
    config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Mailer,
      adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Resend,
      api_key: resend_api_key

    config :cleaner_crm,
           :mailer_from,
           {System.get_env("MAILER_FROM_NAME") || "Desert First Cleaning",
            System.get_env("MAILER_FROM_EMAIL") || "no-reply@#{host}"}
  end

  # ## SSL Support
  #
  # To get SSL working, you will need to add the `https` key

We couldn't find that booking link. It may have expired — please request a new quote.

Your price

{Money.format_cents(@lead.total_cents)}

Locked in from your instant quote — no added fees.

You're booked for {format_date(@lead.scheduled_date)} at {format_time(@lead.start_time)}. Check your email for a link to your client portal.
Confirming your payment — this page will update as soon as it's done.
Your card was declined. Please try a different card below.
That time was just booked by someone else — please pick another slot.
<.form :if={@step == :select_slot} for={@slot_form} id="slot-form" data-test="slot-form" phx-submit="select_slot" > <.input field={@slot_form[:scheduled_date]} type="date" label="Date" /> <.input field={@slot_form[:start_time]} type="time" label="Start time" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Checking...">Continue
<.form :if={@step in [:confirm, :payment_declined]} for={@confirmation_form} id="confirmation-form" data-test="confirmation-form" phx-submit="confirm_booking" >

Cancellation policy: cancel or reschedule at least 24-hour ahead of your visit to avoid a late-cancellation fee.

<.input field={@confirmation_form[:policy_agreed]} type="checkbox" label="I agree to the cancellation policy" data-test="policy-agreement-checkbox" />

""" end def handle_event("select_slot", %{"booking" => params}, socket) do case Booking.select_slot(socket.assigns.lead, params) do {:ok, slotted_lead} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:lead, slotted_lead) |> assign(:step, :confirm)} {:error, changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :slot_form, to_form(changeset, as: :booking))} end end def handle_event("confirm_booking", %{"booking" => params}, socket) do case Booking.confirm_booking(socket.assigns.lead, params) do {:ok, updated} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:lead, updated) |> assign(:step, :payment_pending) |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false)} {:error, :policy_required} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:policy_required, true) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false)} {:error, :slot_unavailable} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:slot_unavailable, true) |> assign(:policy_required, false)} # Defense in depth (issue 4e985412): the slot-selection form # itself now rejects a past date/time, but a slot picked as # "later today" can still go stale by the time the client # reaches this step — send them back to pick a new one rather # than leave them stuck retrying a confirmation that can never # succeed. {:error, :slot_in_past} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:step, :select_slot) |> assign(:slot_form, to_form(Booking.change_slot(socket.assigns.lead), as: :booking)) |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false) |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash( :error, "That time has already passed — please pick another slot." )} # Anything else is a payment/system failure, NOT a slot conflict — # mislabeling it as "someone else booked this" sends the client # hunting for a new time that will fail identically. {:error, reason} -> Logger.error( "Booking confirmation failed for lead #{socket.assigns.lead.id}: " <> inspect(reason) ) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false) |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash( :error, "We could not process your payment. Please try again, or contact us to finish booking." )} end end defp format_date(date), do: Calendar.strftime(date, "%B %-d, %Y") defp format_time(time), do: Calendar.strftime(time, "%-I:%M %p") end

  def handle_event("payment_failed", %{"message" => message}, socket) do

  @doc """
  Pushed every 3s by `.PaymentStatusPoll` while `@step ==
  :payment_pending`, so the page advances the moment the Stripe
  webhook (`CleanerCrm.Booking.receive_payment_webhook/1`) converts or
  declines the lead — without requiring a manual refresh.
  """
  def handle_event("check_payment_status", _params, socket) do
    case Booking.get_lead_by_token(socket.assigns.lead.acceptance_token) do
      %Lead{status: :converted} = refreshed ->
        {:noreply, socket |> assign(:lead, refreshed) |> assign(:step, :confirmed)}

      %Lead{status: :payment_declined} = refreshed ->
        {:noreply, socket |> assign(:lead, refreshed) |> assign(:step, :payment_declined)}

      _still_pending ->
        {:noreply, socket}

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGatewayTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Guards the Live adapter's graceful-degradation behavior: a deploy
  missing `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (any dev machine,
  by design — see `config/dev.exs`) must get `{:error, _}` back from
  every call, never a raised exception that would crash the calling
  LiveView or turn a public controller response into a raw 500.
  """

  use ExUnit.Case, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live

  setup do
    original = Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])

    on_exit(fn ->
      Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, original)
    end)

    Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])
    :ok
  end

  describe "create_payment_intent/1 with no STRIPE_SECRET_KEY configured" do
    test "returns an error tuple instead of raising" do
      assert {:error, %{"code" => "not_configured"}} =
               Live.create_payment_intent(%{amount_cents: 15_000, payment_method: "pm_card_visa"})
    end
  end

  describe "verify_webhook_event/1 with no STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET configured" do
    test "returns an error tuple instead of raising, even with a signature header" do
      conn =
        Plug.Test.conn(:post, "/webhooks/stripe", %{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"})
        |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("stripe-signature", "t=123,v1=deadbeef")
        |> Plug.Conn.assign(:raw_body, ~s({"type":"payment_intent.succeeded"}))

      assert {:error, :invalid_signature} = Live.verify_webhook_event(conn)
    end

    test "returns an error tuple when there's no signature header at all" do
      conn = Plug.Test.conn(:post, "/webhooks/stripe", %{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"})

      assert {:error, :invalid_signature} = Live.verify_webhook_event(conn)
    end
  end
end
