defmodule CleanerCrm.BookingTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 4e985412: `/book/accept/:token`'s slot-selection form
  accepted any date — including years in the past — with zero
  validation, and QA drove a `scheduled_date` of 2020-01-01 all the
  way through card capture into a real scheduled job. Both guards
  added for it are exercised here:

    * `Lead.slot_changeset/3` (via `Booking.select_slot/3`) — the
      form-level guard, rejecting a past date/time outright.
    * `Booking.confirm_booking/3` — the defense-in-depth re-check
      right before a card is charged, in case a slot that was future
      at selection time goes stale (or a lead's slot fields were set
      some other way) by the time the client actually submits payment.

  No spex/BDD story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead,
  mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.TemplatesTest`'s precedent for
  issue-only coverage.

  Also covers the live UAT regression where `public_scope/0` resolved
  the *newest* account unconditionally: three UAT accounts named
  "Desert First Cleaning" existed, and the newest — with a blank rate
  card — silently became the `/book` storefront. `describe
  "public_scope/0"` below drives the fix (the `storefront` flag, with
  an exactly-one-account fallback and `nil` otherwise) directly.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      Booking.create_lead(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  describe "select_slot/3" do
    test "rejects a scheduled_date years in the past" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => "2020-01-01",
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert "must be today or later" in errors_on(changeset).scheduled_date
    end

    test "rejects today's date once the chosen start time has already passed" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      today = Date.utc_today()
      now = DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(
                 lead,
                 %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
                 now
               )

      assert "must be later than the current time" in errors_on(changeset).start_time
    end

    test "accepts a future date" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      future_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)

      assert {:ok, slotted} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(future_date),
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert slotted.scheduled_date == future_date
    end
  end

  describe "confirm_booking/3 (defense in depth against a past slot)" do
    test "refuses a lead whose slot fields are already in the past, without charging a card" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      past_lead = %{lead | scheduled_date: ~D[2020-01-01], start_time: ~T[09:00:00]}

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(past_lead, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
      assert reloaded.status == :accepted
      assert reloaded.stripe_payment_intent_id == nil
    end

    test "refuses a slot picked for later today once that time has passed by confirmation" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      today = Date.utc_today()

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(
          lead,
          %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
          DateTime.new!(today, ~T[13:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
        )

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(
                 slotted,
                 %{"policy_agreed" => "true", "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"},
                 DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
               )
    end

    test "still confirms and moves the lead to payment_pending for a genuinely future slot" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
          "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
          "start_time" => "09:00"
        })

      assert {:ok, updated} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(slotted, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      assert updated.status == :payment_pending
    end
  end

  describe "public_scope/0" do
    test "resolves nil when no account exists at all" do
      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == nil
    end

    test "resolves the only account when exactly one exists and none is flagged" do
      scope = scope_fixture()

      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == scope.active_account_id
    end

    test "resolves nil when multiple accounts exist and none is flagged as the storefront" do
      scope_fixture()
      scope_fixture()

      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == nil
    end

    test "resolves the storefront-flagged account even though a newer account exists" do
      older = scope_fixture()
      {:ok, _updated} = Accounts.set_storefront(older, true)
      _newer = scope_fixture()

      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == older.active_account_id
    end

    test "moving the storefront flag to a different account changes which one resolves" do
      first = scope_fixture()
      second = scope_fixture()

      {:ok, _} = Accounts.set_storefront(first, true)
      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == first.active_account_id

      {:ok, _} = Accounts.set_storefront(second, true)
      assert Booking.public_scope().active_account_id == second.active_account_id

      reloaded_first = Accounts.get_account!(first, first.active_account_id)
      refute reloaded_first.storefront
    end

    test "only an owner may set the storefront flag" do
      owner_scope = scope_fixture()
      admin_user = user_fixture()

      {:ok, _member} =
        Accounts.add_user_to_account(
          owner_scope,
          admin_user.id,
          owner_scope.active_account_id,
          :admin
        )

      admin_scope = %{
        Scope.for_user(admin_user)
        | active_account_id: owner_scope.active_account_id
      }

      assert_raise RuntimeError, ~r/Unauthorized/, fn ->
        Accounts.set_storefront(admin_scope, true)
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.AcceptTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 4e985412: the `/book/accept/:token` slot-selection form
  accepted any date, including years in the past, with zero
  validation — QA drove `scheduled_date=2020-01-01` through card
  capture and it converted into a real scheduled job. No spex/BDD
  story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead. See also
  `CleanerCrm.BookingTest` for the context-level (`Booking`/`Lead`)
  coverage, including the defense-in-depth re-check at confirmation.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      Booking.create_lead(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  test "a past scheduled date is rejected with a clear error and never reaches the confirm step",
       %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    lead = lead_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

    html =
      accept_live
      |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
        booking: %{scheduled_date: "2020-01-01", start_time: "09:00"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

    assert html =~ "must be today or later"
    assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='slot-form']")
    refute has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='confirmation-form']")

    reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
    assert reloaded.scheduled_date == nil
  end

  test "a valid future date advances to the confirmation step", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    lead = lead_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

    accept_live
    |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
      booking: %{
        scheduled_date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
        start_time: "09:00"
      }
    )
    |> render_submit()

    assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='confirmation-form']")
  end
end

  test "a past scheduled date is rejected with a clear error and never reaches the confirm step",
       %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    lead = lead_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

    html =
      accept_live
      |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
        booking: %{scheduled_date: "2020-01-01", start_time: "09:00"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

    assert html =~ "must be today or later"
    assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='slot-form']")
    refute has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='confirmation-form']")

    reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
    assert reloaded.scheduled_date == nil
  end

  test "a valid future date advances to the confirmation step", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    lead = lead_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

    accept_live
    |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
      booking: %{
        scheduled_date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
        start_time: "09:00"
      }
    )
    |> render_submit()

    assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='confirmation-form']")
  end

  describe "card capture fallback (no STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY configured)" do
    test "the confirmation form still carries the hidden test-card field, and submitting it goes straight to payment_pending",
         %{conn: conn} do
      refute Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, :stripe_publishable_key)

      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, accept_live, html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

      accept_live
      |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
        booking: %{
          scheduled_date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
          start_time: "09:00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      html = render(accept_live)
      assert html =~ ~s(name="booking[payment_method]")
      assert html =~ "pm_card_visa"
      refute has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='stripe-payment-form']")

      accept_live
      |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']", booking: %{policy_agreed: "true"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='payment-pending']")
    end
  end

  describe "card capture with Stripe Elements (STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY configured)" do
    setup do
      Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, :stripe_publishable_key, "pk_test_fake")
      on_exit(fn -> Application.delete_env(:cleaner_crm, :stripe_publishable_key) end)
      :ok
    end

    test "the confirmation form omits the hidden test-card field, and agreeing to the policy mounts the Payment Element",
         %{conn: conn} do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

      accept_live
      |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
        booking: %{
          scheduled_date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
          start_time: "09:00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      html = render(accept_live)
      refute html =~ ~s(name="booking[payment_method]")

      accept_live
      |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']", booking: %{policy_agreed: "true"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='stripe-payment-form']")
      assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='stripe-payment-element']")

      html = render(accept_live)
      assert html =~ "pk_test_fake"

      reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
      assert reloaded.status == :payment_pending
      assert reloaded.stripe_payment_intent_id != nil
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story851.Criterion7224Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 851 — Reschedule or cancel a visit within the policy
  Criterion 7224 — On-time cancellation has no fee

  Assumes the same two-step cancel control as criterion 7223's spec:
  `[data-test='cancel-visit-button']` then
  `[data-test='confirm-cancel-button']`, with no
  `[data-test='cancellation-fee-notice']` rendered when the visit is
  outside the notice window.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "cancelling outside the notice window charges no fee" do
    scenario "on-time cancellation has no fee" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the account has a 48-hour notice policy with a $25 late fee", context do
        Fixtures.cancellation_policy_fixture(context.scope, %{
          notice_window_hours: 48,
          late_fee_cents: 2_500,
          same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
        })

        {:ok, context}
      end

      given_ "I have a visit scheduled five days from now, outside the notice window", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 5),
            start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "I cancel the visit and confirm", context do
        {:ok, visit_live, _html} =
          live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/visits/#{context.job.id}")

        visit_live
        |> element("[data-test='cancel-visit-button']")
        |> render_click()

        refute has_element?(visit_live, "[data-test='cancellation-fee-notice']")

        visit_live
        |> element("[data-test='confirm-cancel-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :visit_live, visit_live)}
      end

      then_ "the visit is cancelled with no fee charged", context do
        html = render(context.visit_live)

        assert html =~ "Cancelled"
        refute html =~ ~r/fee/i

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

1	defmodule Mix.Tasks.Spex do
2	  @shortdoc "Run executable specifications (spex)"
3	  @moduledoc """
4	  Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.
5	
6	  SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve as
7	  both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development workflows.
8	
9	  Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup blocks:
10	  - setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
11	  - setup: State reset between tests
12	  - Context passing between test steps
13	  - Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)
14	
15	  ## Usage
16	
17	      mix spex                    # Run all spex files
18	      mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
19	      mix spex --help             # Show this help
20	
21	  ## Options
22	
23	      --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
24	      --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
25	      --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
26	      --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
27	      --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
28	      --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
29	      --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
30	      --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
31	                      Can be specified multiple times
32	      --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
33	      --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
34	      --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)
35	
36	  ## Examples
37	
38	      mix spex
39	      mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
40	      mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
41	      mix spex --verbose
42	      mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
43	      mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution
44	      mix spex --speed medium --verbose  # Medium speed with detailed output
45	      mix spex --trace            # Show detailed test execution
46	      mix spex test/spex/file.exs --trace
47	      mix spex --slowest 5        # Show timing for 5 slowest tests
48	
49	  ## Configuration
50	
51	  You can configure spex behavior in your config files:
52	
53	      config :sexy_spex,
54	        manual_mode: false,
55	        step_delay: 0
56	
57	  Application lifecycle is handled in individual spex files using setup_all blocks.
58	
59	  ## Important: Test Environment Setup
60	
61	  To ensure spex runs in the test environment with proper module compilation,
62	  add this to your project's mix.exs:
63	
64	      def project do
65	        [
66	          # ... other config
67	          preferred_cli_env: [
68	            spex: :test
69	          ]
70	        ]
71	      end
72	
73	  This ensures that `mix spex` always runs in the test environment and compiles
74	  modules with test-specific code paths (e.g., test/support directories).
75	
76	  """
77	
78	  use Mix.Task
79	
80	  alias Mix.Compilers.Test, as: CT
81	
82	  @default_pattern "test/spex/**/*_spex.exs"
83	  @default_timeout 60_000

85	  def run(args) do
86	    # Ensure we're running in test environment for spex
87	    # Note: This task should have preferred_cli_env set to :test in mix.exs
88	    # of projects using spex to ensure proper compilation
89	
90	    # Compile the project to ensure test environment modules are loaded
91	    Mix.Task.run("compile")
92	
93	    # Start the application like mix test does
94	    # This ensures all applications and their dependencies are started
95	    Mix.Task.run("app.start")
96	
97	    # Pre-process args to handle --jsonl without value (convert to --jsonl=default)
98	    args = preprocess_jsonl_arg(args)
99	
100	    {opts, files, _} = OptionParser.parse(args,
101	      switches: [
102	        only_spex: :boolean,
103	        pattern: :string,
104	        verbose: :boolean,
105	        timeout: :integer,
106	        help: :boolean,
107	        manual: :boolean,
108	        speed: :string,
109	        trace: :boolean,
110	        slowest: :integer,
111	        formatter: :keep,
112	        jsonl: :string,
113	        stale: :boolean,
114	        force: :boolean
115	      ],
116	      aliases: [
117	        h: :help,
118	        v: :verbose,
119	        m: :manual,
120	        s: :speed,
121	        t: :trace,
122	        f: :formatter,
123	        j: :jsonl
124	      ]
125	    )
126	
127	    if opts[:help] do
128	      Mix.shell().info(@moduledoc)
129	      return()
130	    end
131	
132	    # Find spex files
133	    spex_files = find_spex_files(files, opts)

229	  end

defmodule Mix.Tasks.Spex do
  @shortdoc "Run executable specifications (spex)"
  @moduledoc """
  Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

  SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve as
  both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development workflows.

  Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup blocks:
  - setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  - setup: State reset between tests
  - Context passing between test steps
  - Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

  ## Usage

      mix spex                    # Run all spex files
      mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
      mix spex --help             # Show this help

  ## Options

      --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
      --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
      --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
      --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
      --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
      --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
      --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
      --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                      Can be specified multiple times
      --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
      --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
      --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

  ## Examples

      mix spex
      mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
      mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
      mix spex --verbose
      mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
      mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution
      mix spex --speed medium --verbose  # Medium speed with detailed output
      mix spex --trace            # Show detailed test execution
      mix spex test/spex/file.exs --trace
      mix spex --slowest 5        # Show timing for 5 slowest tests

  ## Configuration

  You can configure spex behavior in your config files:

      config :sexy_spex,
        manual_mode: false,
        step_delay: 0

  Application lifecycle is handled in individual spex files using setup_all blocks.

  ## Important: Test Environment Setup

  To ensure spex runs in the test environment with proper module compilation,
  add this to your project's mix.exs:

      def project do
        [
          # ... other config
          preferred_cli_env: [
            spex: :test
          ]
        ]
      end

  This ensures that `mix spex` always runs in the test environment and compiles
  modules with test-specific code paths (e.g., test/support directories).

  """

  use Mix.Task

  alias Mix.Compilers.Test, as: CT

  @default_pattern "test/spex/**/*_spex.exs"
  @default_timeout 60_000

  def run(args) do
    # Ensure we're running in test environment for spex
    # Note: This task should have preferred_cli_env set to :test in mix.exs
    # of projects using spex to ensure proper compilation

    # Compile the project to ensure test environment modules are loaded
    Mix.Task.run("compile")

    # Start the application like mix test does
    # This ensures all applications and their dependencies are started
    Mix.Task.run("app.start")

    # Pre-process args to handle --jsonl without value (convert to --jsonl=default)
    args = preprocess_jsonl_arg(args)

    {opts, files, _} = OptionParser.parse(args,
      switches: [
        only_spex: :boolean,
        pattern: :string,
        verbose: :boolean,
        timeout: :integer,
        help: :boolean,
        manual: :boolean,
        speed: :string,
        trace: :boolean,
        slowest: :integer,
        formatter: :keep,
        jsonl: :string,
        stale: :boolean,
        force: :boolean
      ],
      aliases: [
        h: :help,
        v: :verbose,
        m: :manual,
        s: :speed,
        t: :trace,
        f: :formatter,
        j: :jsonl
      ]
    )

    if opts[:help] do
      Mix.shell().info(@moduledoc)
      return()
    end

    # Find spex files
    spex_files = find_spex_files(files, opts)

    if Enum.empty?(spex_files) do
      pattern = opts[:pattern] || @default_pattern
      Mix.shell().info("No spex files found matching pattern: #{pattern}")
      Mix.shell().info("Try: mix spex --help")
      # Exit early if no files found
      System.halt(0)
    end

    # Configure spex execution
    configure_spex_mode(opts)

    if opts[:verbose] do
      Mix.shell().info("Running #{length(spex_files)} spex file(s)...")
    end

    # Run spex tests with ExUnit
    run_tests_with_exunit(spex_files, opts)
  end

  defp return, do: :ok

  # Handle --jsonl without a value: if the next arg looks like a file, don't consume it
  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg(args) do
    preprocess_jsonl_arg(args, [])
  end

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg([], acc), do: Enum.reverse(acc)

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg(["--jsonl" | rest], acc) do
    case rest do
      [next | remaining] when is_binary(next) ->
        # If next arg starts with - or ends with .exs, treat --jsonl as having default value
        if String.starts_with?(next, "-") or String.ends_with?(next, ".exs") do
          preprocess_jsonl_arg(rest, ["--jsonl=spex_failures.jsonl" | acc])
        else
          # Next arg is the jsonl path, skip it
          preprocess_jsonl_arg(remaining, ["--jsonl=#{next}" | acc])
        end
      [] ->
        # --jsonl at end with no value
        Enum.reverse(["--jsonl=spex_failures.jsonl" | acc])
    end
  end

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg(["-j" | rest], acc) do
    preprocess_jsonl_arg(["--jsonl" | rest], acc)
  end

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg([arg | rest], acc) do
    preprocess_jsonl_arg(rest, [arg | acc])
  end

  defp find_spex_files([], opts) do
    # No specific files provided, use pattern
    pattern = opts[:pattern] || @default_pattern
    Path.wildcard(pattern)
  end

  defp find_spex_files(files, _opts) do
    # Specific files provided
    Enum.filter(files, &File.exists?/1)
  end

  defp configure_spex_mode(opts) do
    # Quiet by default; verbose opts in
    unless opts[:verbose] do
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :quiet, true)
    end

    # Configure JSONL output if requested
    if opts[:jsonl] do
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :jsonl_enabled, true)
      path = if is_binary(opts[:jsonl]) and opts[:jsonl] != "true",
        do: opts[:jsonl],
        else: "spex_failures.jsonl"
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :jsonl_path, path)
      # Clear file at start
      File.write!(path, "")
    end

    # Set manual mode if requested
    if opts[:manual] do
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :manual_mode, true)
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 0)
      if opts[:verbose], do: Mix.shell().info("Manual mode enabled - you'll be prompted at each step")
    else
      # Configure speed if provided
      configure_speed(opts[:speed], opts[:verbose])
    end
  end

  defp configure_speed(nil, verbose), do: configure_speed("fast", verbose)
  defp configure_speed("fast", _verbose) do
    Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 0)
  end
  defp configure_speed("medium", verbose) do
    Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 1000)
    if verbose, do: Mix.shell().info("Medium speed mode - 1s delays between steps")
  end
  defp configure_speed("slow", verbose) do
    Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 2500)
    if verbose, do: Mix.shell().info("Slow speed mode - 2.5s delays between steps")
  end
  defp configure_speed(invalid, _verbose) do
    Mix.shell().error("Invalid speed: #{invalid}. Valid options: fast, medium, slow")
    System.halt(1)
  end

  defp parse_formatters(opts) do
    formatters =
      opts
      |> Keyword.get_values(:formatter)
      |> Enum.map(&parse_formatter_module/1)

    if Enum.empty?(formatters) do
      [ExUnit.CLIFormatter]
    else
      formatters
    end
  end

  defp parse_formatter_module(name) do
    module = Module.concat([name])

    unless Code.ensure_loaded?(module) do
      Mix.shell().error("Could not load formatter module: #{name}")
      System.halt(1)
    end

    module
  end

  defp run_tests_with_exunit(spex_files, opts) do
    if opts[:stale] do
      run_with_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts)
    else
      run_without_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts)
    end
  end

  defp run_without_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts) do
    opts
    |> build_exunit_config()
    |> ExUnit.start()

    load_spex_files(spex_files, opts)

    ExUnit.run()
    |> handle_results()
  end

  defp run_with_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts) do
    exunit_config = build_exunit_config(opts)
    ExUnit.start(exunit_config)

    test_paths = spex_test_paths()
    test_elixirc_options = Mix.Project.config()[:test_elixirc_options] || []

    case CT.require_and_run(spex_files, test_paths, test_elixirc_options, opts) do
      {:ok, results} ->
        handle_results(results)

      :noop ->
        if opts[:verbose] do
          Mix.shell().info("No stale spex files")
        end

        System.halt(0)
    end
  end

  defp spex_test_paths do
    # Return the directory containing spex files so the stale manifest
    # can find test_helper.exs (falls back gracefully if not present)
    ["test/spex"]
  end

  defp build_exunit_config(opts) do
    timeout = opts[:timeout] || @default_timeout
    formatters = parse_formatters(opts)

    config = [
      colors: [enabled: true],
      formatters: formatters,
      timeout: timeout
    ]

    config
    |> maybe_enable_trace(opts[:verbose])
    |> maybe_enable_trace(opts[:trace])
    |> maybe_set_slowest(opts[:slowest])
  end

  defp maybe_enable_trace(config, true), do: Keyword.put(config, :trace, true)
  defp maybe_enable_trace(config, _), do: config

  defp maybe_set_slowest(config, n) when is_integer(n) and n > 0,
    do: Keyword.put(config, :slowest, n)

  defp maybe_set_slowest(config, _), do: config

  # When the :spex compiler (from client_utils) already compiled these files,
  # suppress "redefining module" warnings — we still need Code.require_file
  # so modules register with ExUnit.
  defp load_spex_files(spex_files, _opts) do
    already_compiled = spex_already_compiled?()
    if already_compiled, do: Code.put_compiler_option(:ignore_module_conflict, true)

    Enum.each(spex_files, fn file ->
      try do
        Code.require_file(file)
      rescue
        error ->
          Mix.shell().error("Failed to load #{file}: #{Exception.message(error)}")
          System.halt(1)
      end
    end)

    if already_compiled, do: Code.put_compiler_option(:ignore_module_conflict, false)
  end

  defp spex_already_compiled? do
    :persistent_term.get({Mix.Tasks.Compile.Spex, :diagnostics}, nil) != nil
  end

  defp handle_results(result) do
    verbose = !Application.get_env(:sexy_spex, :quiet, true)

    case result do
      %{failures: 0} ->
        if verbose, do: Mix.shell().info("All spex passed!")
        System.halt(0)

      %{failures: failures} when failures > 0 ->
        if verbose, do: Mix.shell().error("#{failures} spex failed")
        System.halt(1)

      _ ->
        if verbose, do: Mix.shell().error("Spex execution encountered errors")
        System.halt(1)
    end
  end

end

content.text:
I've implemented real Stripe Elements card capture for the booking-acceptance page and sent a summary to the team lead. Here's the recap:

**How it works:** When `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` isn't configured (dev/test, always), the page behaves exactly as before — hidden `pm_card_visa` field, synchronous confirmed intent. When it is configured (prod), the confirmation form omits that field, `Booking.confirm_booking/3` creates an *unconfirmed* Stripe intent and returns a `client_secret`, and the LiveView mounts a Payment Element via a colocated `.StripePaymentElement` JS hook (following the existing `CmsScreenshot` hook pattern already in this codebase rather than introducing a separate `assets/js` file). A second `.PaymentStatusPoll` hook polls every 3 seconds so the page flips to confirmed/declined live once the webhook processes it, without touching `Quote.ex` or adding PubSub.

**Files touched:** `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/booking_live/accept.ex`, `lib/cleaner_crm/booking.ex` (confirm_booking/submit_payment only), `lib/cleaner_crm/billing/stripe_gateway.ex` + `live.ex` + `test.ex`, `config/runtime.exs`, and three test files (`test/cleaner_crm/booking_test.exs`, `test/cleaner_crm_web/live/booking_live/accept_test.exs`, `test/cleaner_crm/billing/stripe_gateway_test.exs`).

**Verification:** clean compile with `--warnings-as-errors`, full test suite 317/317 passing (up from 308), spex suite 143/143 passing, `mix assets.build` succeeds with both hooks bundled into `app.js`, and `mix format` shows no diffs. One unrelated spex test (visit-cancellation fees) flaked once during a combined run but passed on every other run both with and without my changes — confirmed as pre-existing flakiness, not a regression.

This needs a release rebuild since it adds the `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` config plumbing and a new JS hook.
